The Stripe at the Bottom of the Pool

泳池底下的那条线 · 650 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A recreation center opened a heated pool beside its gym. Nina signed up for a swimming lesson on her day off. She could swim a short distance, but a knee injury made a vigorous kick painful. Her instructor wanted her to begin with a warm-up in the shallow lane. At the locker she found a brown cap, a towel, and a plastic bracelet with the wrong lesson number. She put on the cap without reading the bracelet. On the pool deck she followed a group preparing for a timed workout.

2The swimmers bent forward. Nina copied them, then raised her heel off the tile. The instructor saw her brace her thigh. Her bracelet belonged to a more vigorous class. The mistake was embarrassing, and Nina thought a swimsuit had somehow made her look like a regular competitor. The instructor did not scold her. He pointed to a striped rail and showed her where to hang her bathrobe. Her actual lesson began by a shallow step.

3In the correct lane Nina held a foam board with both thumbs over the top. The instructor asked her to breathe out and let her toes turn inward slightly. She tried a small kick. It pulled near the knee, while her belly and calf stayed relaxed. She rarely swam far. She would stare at the floor, then look up too sharply. A reflective stripe let her rest after a few strokes. Besides the distance, she could check whether she clenched her teeth or tightened her grip.

4Nina fixed her gaze on the stripe and held her breath. As she looked upwards, a splash struck her face. She grabbed the rope with a fist and stared down. A boy in the next lane slapped the water. Nina realized she had taken that vigorous movement as a model. The instructor let her wait until her jaw and hands relaxed. A steady rhythm made the same stretch less tough, and she finished without feeling miserable.

5A keen pupil had grown bored with an indoor workout. He usually trained at a stadium and thought a gentle lap would not motivate him. Nina suggested a floating ball they could move with a light touch. He laughed when it bounced back. After a bunch of attempts, he moved it to the stripe without splashing. There was enjoyment in controlling the motion. They could turn that into a habit before they made speed their only goal.

6While they rested, a staff member brought the original class schedule. The gym listed a treadmill workout, a roller class, and a swim practice on the same board. It used nearly identical symbols for all three. Nina had gotten as far as the wrong pool. She hoped other beginners could avoid that awful moment. She suggested showing a picture of the equipment and spelling out the class name. That small change could reduce embarrassment for someone who was already tired from finding the building.

7At the end the changing room was a mess. A wet glove lay beside a pile of shorts. Nina found the first bracelet near the shower and compared its two-digit code with the printed class list. The center used the same colors for exercise groups and swimming levels. She suggested changing the locker tags to include the lane number in words. A member of staff brought a marker and fixed the sign before the next group came in.

8The following week Nina arrived in a hoodie and took her usual board. She tightened the buckle on her bag, checked the bracelet, and went to the stripe. A new pupil said the exercise looked boring. Nina said she had once made it more frustrating by judging every move by speed. Familiarity with a short stretch made gentle exertion easier to tolerate. She was glad to show him how to stop there. Perseverance could mean repeating a comfortable movement, then choosing the next one.

四级汇总词汇 · 36中文译文

泳池底下的那条线

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一家活动中心在健身房旁开了个温水泳池。妮娜趁休息日报了游泳课。她能游一小段，但膝盖有伤，腿蹬得太用力就会疼。教练想让她先到浅水泳道热身。她在储物柜旁找到一顶棕色泳帽、一条毛巾和一条印错课程号的塑料手环。她只顾戴上帽子，没看手环。来到池边，她跟上了一组正准备计时训练的人。

2那群游泳的人弯腰向前。妮娜照着做，把脚跟抬离瓷砖。教练注意到她大腿绷得很紧。原来，她的手环属于强度更大的课。妮娜很尴尬，还以为自己一穿泳衣，看起来就像经常比赛的人。教练没有责怪她。他指着带条纹的栏杆，告诉她浴袍挂在哪儿。她真正的课在浅水台阶旁开始。

3回到正确的泳道，妮娜用两只拇指压住泡沫浮板的上沿。教练请她呼气，把脚趾稍微转向内侧。她轻轻蹬了一下。膝盖附近有牵拉感，肚子和小腿却放松着。她平时很少游远，总是先盯着池底，再猛地抬头。池底的反光条提醒她划几下就可以停下来歇。除了距离，她还能留意自己有没有咬紧牙关、抓得太紧。

4妮娜盯住反光条，屏住了气。一抬头，水花就打到她脸上。她一把抓住分道绳，往下看。旁边泳道一个男孩把水拍得很响。她才发现，自己刚刚照着那个用力的动作学了。教练让她等到下巴和手都放松，再接着游。节奏一稳，同一段就没那么难了。她游完时，身体也没觉得难受。

5有个热衷锻炼的学生早就嫌室内训练无聊。他平常在体育场练习，觉得慢慢游一圈提不起劲。妮娜提议用一个浮球，看能不能轻轻把它推过去。球弹回来时，他笑了。试了好几次之后，他终于让球移到那条线的位置，水都没溅起来。能控制好动作，本身就有乐趣。他们可以先练成习惯，再去追求速度。

6休息时，一位工作人员拿来了原来的课程表。健身房把跑步机训练、轮滑课和游泳练习写在同一块板上，三项的图标几乎一样。妮娜已经走错过泳池，她希望其他初学者免受那阵窘迫。她建议画出会用到的器材，再写清楚课程全名。有人光是找对楼就已经累了，这个小改动至少可以省掉一次尴尬。

7下课时，更衣室乱成一团。一只湿手套掉在一堆短裤旁。妮娜在淋浴间附近找到了最初的那条手环，拿上面的两位数编号对照打印的名单。中心用同一套颜色区分健身组和游泳级别。她建议直接在储物柜的标签上写出泳道号。一位工作人员拿来记号笔，在下一组进来之前改好了标牌。

8下一周，妮娜穿着连帽衫来上课，拿起平常用的浮板。她扣紧包扣，检查手环，来到那条线旁。一位新学员觉得这个练习很无聊。妮娜说，自己以前什么都用速度来衡量，练起来反而挫败。熟悉了这一小段，轻轻用力也就没那么难受了。她乐意指给他看在哪里停。坚持有时就是先把一个舒服的动作重复练好，再决定下一步。
